narrative: In the 2020s, Black and African women's hairstyles and hair culture continue to thrive, building on decades of resistance against Eurocentric beauty standards. The natural hair movement remains a powerful force, celebrating the diversity of textured hair in all its forms - waves, curls, kinks, and more. Hairstyles like afros, cornrows, and locs are staples of African diasporic culture, with each style carrying its own rich history and significance. Protective hairstyles, such as box braids and Bantu knots, are essential for preserving the integrity of Afro-textured hair. While the Jheri curl may have been a popular chemical treatment in previous decades, it is not mentioned as being relevant to this era's hairstyles. Unfortunately, documentation on this specific decade is limited within the source material, but what we do know highlights the resilience and creativity of Black and African women in defining their own beauty standards and embracing their unique hair textures.
